$comment: The Mlola Render catalog, written by hand: which components an agent may ask for, and which props each takes. Fixed values (variant, tone, size…) are not written here: `from` names the component prop they are read from, so the catalog cannot offer a value the component no longer has. scripts/build-render-catalog.mjs resolves this file into render-rules.json (what the validator reads) and render-catalog.json (the A2UI catalog). See docs/render.md.
title: Mlola Render catalog
description: Mlola UI components for interfaces an agent composes at runtime. Every component is accessible by construction and follows the surface's theme; an agent picks named values (tone, variant, size) and never writes a color, size or class.

Stack.description: Places its children in a column with the theme's spacing. Use it as the root of most surfaces.

children.description: The components inside, top to bottom.

Row.description: Places its children side by side and wraps them on a narrow screen. Use it for a row of buttons or badges.

children.description: The components inside, start to end.

Grid.description: Places its children in equal columns that collapse to one column on a phone.

children.description: The components inside, in reading order.

columns.description: How many columns on a wide screen. Leave it out to fit as many as the width allows.

Heading.description: A heading. Levels follow the page outline: never skip a level going deeper.

level.description: The outline level, 1 to 6. Inside a chat a surface usually starts at 2.

text.description: The words. Line breaks are kept; markup is shown as text.

Card.description: Groups related content on a surface of its own.

variant.description: How the card stands off the page.

Alert.description: A message about the surface: a confirmation, a warning or an error. Warnings and errors interrupt a screen reader; calmer tones are announced politely.

text.description: What happened and what to do about it.

variant.description: A card, or a tinted band across the surface.

EmptyState.description: Says that there is nothing here yet and what to do next.

title.description: What is empty, in a few words.

children.description: Actions, usually one or two Buttons.

size.description: inline inside a surface, page when it fills one.

Tabs.description: Shows one panel at a time, chosen from a row of tabs. Its children are Tab components.

label.description: What the tabs choose between, for a screen reader.

variant.description: The look of the tab row.

Tab.description: One tab of a Tabs: its name and its panel.

Accordion.description: A list of sections that open and close. Its children are AccordionItem components.

type.description: single keeps one section open at a time; multiple lets several stay open.

AccordionItem.description: One section of an Accordion: its title and its content.

title.description: The section's title, which opens and closes it.

Input.description: A one-line text field with its label.

label.description: The field's name, shown above it and read by a screen reader.

value.description: Bind it to the data model ({"path": "/form/email"}) so the value comes back with the action.

type.description: The kind of text, which picks the phone keyboard and the browser's checks.

placeholder.description: An example of what to type. Never a replacement for the label.

required.description: The form cannot be sent without it.

disabled.description: Shows the control but does not let it change.

size.description: The control size from the density scale.

variant.description: How the field sits on its surface.

Textarea.description: A text field for several lines, with its label.

value.description: Bind it to the data model so the value comes back with the action.

placeholder.description: An example of what to type. Never the only label.

hint.description: A short help line under the field.

rows.description: How many lines show before it scrolls.

required.description: The person must fill it in before the action is sent; a screen reader says so.

disabled.description: Shows the control but does not let it change.

Select.description: Picks one value from a list that opens on demand. Use RadioGroup when there are only two to five options and room to show them.

value.description: The chosen option's value. Bind it to the data model.

required.description: The person must fill it in before the action is sent; a screen reader says so.

disabled.description: Shows the control but does not let it change.

size.description: The control size from the density scale.

RadioGroup.description: Picks one value from options that are all visible.

value.description: The chosen option's value. Bind it to the data model.

orientation.description: Options stacked or in a row.

required.description: The person must fill it in before the action is sent; a screen reader says so.

disabled.description: Shows the control but does not let it change.

Checkbox.description: A yes or no choice with its label.

checked.description: Bind it to the data model so the choice comes back with the action.

description.description: More about the choice, under the label.

required.description: The person must fill it in before the action is sent; a screen reader says so.

disabled.description: Shows the control but does not let it change.

Switch.description: Turns a setting on or off right away.

checked.description: Bind it to the data model.

disabled.description: Shows the control but does not let it change.

size.description: The control size from the density scale.

Slider.description: Picks a number in a range by dragging or with the arrow keys.

value.description: Bind it to the data model.

step.description: How far one arrow press moves it.

disabled.description: Shows the control but does not let it change.

size.description: The control size from the density scale.

DatePicker.description: A date field that opens a calendar and picks one day. The reader sees the date in their own format; the value is an ISO date.

value.description: The chosen day as an ISO date, like "2026-10-12". Bind it to the data model so it comes back with the action.

min.description: The earliest day that can be picked.

max.description: The latest day that can be picked.

required.description: The form cannot be sent without it.

disabled.description: Shows the control but does not let it change.

Button.description: Sends an action back to the agent. Its text says what happens ("Create workspace", not "Submit").

action.description: The event sent when it is pressed.

variant.description: primary for the main action of a surface, one at most.

size.description: Icon-only buttons are not in the catalog: every button has words.

width.description: auto fits the words, full fills the container.

disabled.description: Shows the control but does not let it change.

Badge.description: A short label for a status or a count.

text.description: The badge's words, a few at most.

variant.description: How strongly the badge stands out.

size.description: The control size from the density scale.

Progress.description: Shows how far along something is.

label.description: What is in progress, for a screen reader.

value.description: How far along, from 0 to max.

showLabel.description: Shows the percentage beside the bar.

size.description: The control size from the density scale.

Avatar.description: A person or a team shown by their initials.

name.description: The full name: the initials come from it and a screen reader reads it.

status.description: A presence dot, announced with the name.

Table.description: Rows of data under named columns. Cells hold text and numbers.

caption.description: What the table shows, read first by a screen reader.

columns.description: Each {"key", "label", "align"?}: key names the row field the column shows.

rows.description: An array of objects keyed by column key, or a path to one in the data model.

borrowed.$comment: What agents reach for from A2UI's basic catalog that Mlola does not take, and what to use instead. The check answers with these words; the guide lists them up front. A prop hint is keyed by the prop, by Component.prop, or by Component.prop=value for a value the component does not have.

components.Image: Say what matters in Text, or leave the image out.
components.Icon: Every control has words: put the meaning in the text, or in a Badge.
components.Video: Describe it in Text, or leave it out.
components.AudioPlayer: Describe it in Text, or leave it out.
components.Modal: A surface shows inline, with no dialog. Put the content on the surface, or in a Tab or an AccordionItem to keep it out of the way.
components.Divider: Spacing comes from Stack, and a Card or a Heading separates groups. Leave the divider out.

props.weight: Children share space by the theme's layout. For equal columns use a Grid.
props.justify: A Row or a Stack places its children by the theme's layout. For equal columns use a Grid.
props.align: A Row or a Stack places its children by the theme's layout. For equal columns use a Grid.
props.Stack.direction: A Stack is a column. For side by side use a Row.
props.Text.variant: Text is one style of paragraph. For a heading use a Heading with "level".
props.Button.child: A Button holds its words in "text", not in a child component.
props.Tabs.tabs: A Tabs' "children" are Tab components, each with a "label" and "children".
props.Checkbox.value: A Checkbox's state is "checked": true, false or {"path": "/…"}.
props.Switch.value: A Switch's state is "checked": true, false or {"path": "/…"}.
props.Input.validationRegexp: Client-side checks are not in the Mlola catalog yet. Mark the field "required", and check the value when the action arrives.
props.Select.variant: A Select picks one value. For several choices, use a Checkbox for each.
props.Select.displayStyle: A Select always opens a list. For options that are all visible use a RadioGroup.
props.Select.filterable: A Select lists its options as they are. Keep to the ones that matter, at most 100.
props.Input.variant=longText: For several lines use a Textarea.
props.Input.variant=number: Numbers are not a field type yet. Use a Slider for a number in a range, or an Input with a hint.
props.Input.variant=shortText: An Input is one line already, so leave "variant" out.
props.Button.variant=default: For a button beside the main one use "secondary".
props.Button.variant=borderless: For a quiet button use "subtle" or "link".
props.DatePicker.enableDate: A DatePicker always picks a day, so leave "enableDate" out.
props.DatePicker.enableTime: Times are not in the Mlola catalog yet: a DatePicker picks a day. Ask for the time in an Input with a hint.
